A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same learning-rule inference framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated learning-rule recovery experiments and behavioral modeling of 12 IBL mice, including held-out prediction results in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for decision-model mismatch and a Transformer–RNN comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed DNNGLM/RNNGLM update equations, GLM choice model, and likelihood objective remain unchanged. Additional IBL inputs are newly documented without establishing a revision to the existing fits; the supplementary architectural and decision-model comparisons do not replace the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds a synthetic scenario with context-dependent multiplicative integration of left and right cues, extending the represented decision processes beyond the previous simulations. The IBL dataset and existing simulation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: v1 promises a systematic sequence-model comparison; v2 Appendix D reports an actual Transformer-variant comparison against the RNN. Comparator membership in Tables 1–2, including tinyRNN and REINFORCE variants, is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 qualifies v1's general psychometric-initialization description by specifying known initial weights for short simulations and estimated weights for the long-sequence example. This revises the reported setting without establishing reruns. Table 7 also introduces matched multiplicative versus misspecified additive decision-model conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds a decision-model misspecification test in Table 7 and a completed architecture comparison in Appendix D. Appendix C also reports unchanged conclusions when extra IBL inputs are omitted or batching changes. Existing noise, initialization, pooling, and history analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions describe four seeds for cross-validation likelihoods, three seeds for Figure 12, paired t-tests across mice, and the same uncertainty summaries. The additional architecture-comparison p-value is a new result, without a newly described statistical procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports relative RMSE of 1.00 with the correct decision model versus 1.62 under mismatch. Appendix D reports comparable fully trained Transformer/RNN performance, with p = 0.744. Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results; Figure 2C changes its axis display rather than its data.

T1.justification: Table 7 adds formal definitions of a context-gated multiplicative decision model and its additive GLM misspecification. This is a limited addition of mathematical model assumptions; Appendix A's identifiability proposition and proof and Appendix B's learning-rule derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 4 no longer advertises negative baseline and decision-outcome asymmetry as headline contributions, emphasizing multi-trial reward-history dependence instead. The negative-baseline finding is now explicitly credited to prior work. The central inference, recovery, and prediction claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 now grounds the fixed-decision-model limitation in observed degradation for multiplicative processes. Appendix D adds the hypothesis that the small animal sample explains comparable Transformer/RNN performance and distinguishes preliminary limited-training observations from the final comparison.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository address and documents binary daybreak/stimulus-side inputs, simulation batch size, joint IBL training, and the initialization exception for short simulations. These improve implementation disclosure; most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and runtime details were already present.

R1.justification: v2 adds Geadah and Pillow (2025), crediting its negative-baseline terminology/finding, and four references concerning biologically motivated learning and plasticity. The broader positioning relative to parametric behavioral models, synaptic-rule inference, and meta-learning remains.

P1.justification: The title is shortened and the abstract rewritten to explain the GLM policy and history-dependent updates more directly. Targeted prose revisions, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist are added, while the main scientific section order and Appendices A–D remain.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts NeurIPS formatting, changing typography, title treatment, text width, figure sizing, and float placement. Table 7 is added, existing supplementary tables and figures are rearranged, and Figure 2C switches from explicit log-values to logarithmic axes. Most scientific figure panels are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 empirically substantiates the previously qualitative decision-model limitation through Table 7 and improves reproducibility documentation through initialization clarification, input/batching details, and a code address. Clearer attribution also improves research positioning. The central evidence and identifiability argument remain unchanged, and the new comparisons receive limited methodological detail, so the overall gain is modest.
